## The notation

Studyflow
: The notation itself, a standard for describing and coordinating experiments.*Modeler* is the authoring app, where you design, validate, import, and export studyflow files. *Runner* is the execution app, where you run studyflows and record what happens. There can be multiple runners and the study's `runtime` or pre-defined attributes in the schemas pick between them. 

study
: What a studyflow describes. In the file, the root carrying the `studyflow:Study` extension: the process, or the collaboration once the study is drawn in pools. It is one study either way: adding the first pool or deleting the last changes the kind of the root, never the study's id, name, or settings. A studyflow file is a single source of truth for one study (or experiment). The study is the *prospective* side of the file, and the *retrospective* side is the record of what actually happened when it ran and it is describe by provenance history.

element
: Anything in the diagram. Elements are either nodes or edges. Nodes are activities, events, gateways, and containers. Edges are sequence flows and data associations.

activity
: A node that performs some work when the execution reaches it. A *task* is the most basic kind of activity. Distinct from `prov:Activity`, which is an entry of the provenance.

attribute
: A named value on an element. For example, `name` is an attribute on every element, and `implementation` is and attribute on every activity.

sequence flow
: A solid edge for control flow, showing what happens after what.


data association
: A dotted edge for data flow, showing what an element reads and what it writes. What a data edge may state is called binding, written `slot = selection`. The slot names which argument of the target element the value fills, and the selection names which value arrives from the source.

event
: A node that marks something happening: start, end, a moment, a condition becoming true.

gateway
: A node where a decision is made about which path to take next. Each kind decides differently: by conditions on the edges, by a random sample (`RandomGateway`), or by criteria (`EligibilityGateway`). As in BPMN, a gateway routes the flow when the study runs; the research gateways add ways to decide, a seeded draw or a screening rule.

actor
: Who or what takes part in a study: a person, a program, a device, or, with the agentic skill, a model. One actor is drawn as a pool, and named on a band of each task it takes. In the file an actor is a `bpmn:Participant`, BPMN's word for a party to a collaboration, which is why a collaboration lists its pools under `participants`.

pool
: The drawing of one actor, not of a group. A pool holds a flow: the study's own flow, what is presented and in what order, becomes a pool once another actor is drawn, and a run walks it once per participant. Any other pool holds its actor's own flow, how it does what it does. A person has none to draw: their pool is empty, what BPMN calls a black box, drawn collapsed as a strip with the name across it, and they answer at the screen; a step inside such a pool, if any, is what they do on their own with no software between, BPMN's manual task. A program's pool is empty too when a skill plays it, a model or a bot, or holds the steps the program performs, as a robot's does. Two pools that deal with each other make the diagram a collaboration, and they talk only along message flows. `multiplicity` makes a run take a pool's flow once per instance.

band
: One of the two strips of a task drawn as an exchange: the actor on top presents, the actor below takes it, and the one that starts the exchange is drawn light. A cognitive task names only its taker, since the task itself presents. Typing a name no actor has on a band declares a new actor, drawn as a collapsed pool.

lane
: A division of one flow into roles or phases, inside a pool or an expanded sub-process: the experimenter's steps and the participant's in a protocol figure, or screening, training and testing. A lane is a partition of the drawing, not a step: nothing waits on it, and a run walks straight through it. Where the other side acts on its own, draw a pool instead.

participant
: One person or agent going through a run: one instance of the pool they walk. A browser session is one participant, and `?participant=k` in its link makes it the k-th, so it draws at each random gateway what the k-th instance of a local run draws.

checklist
: Todo items carried on any element. The Checklist view shows what is done (e.g., reported) and what is still to be done (e.g., missing data). The checklist is a *projection* of the diagram. The main use case is to keep track of what is done and what is still to be done, and to make sure that the study is complete and reproducible.

projection (or view)
: A different representation of the diagram. Projections are not a new diagram, but a different way to look at the same diagram. They are codes that visualize some aspects of the studyflow diagram by keeping some elements/attributes of the diagram. A projection never adds or renames, so it cannot modify the study. Currently, five projections are supported: Study, Schedule, Checklist, Provenance, and Figure.

## Running a study

run
: One walk through the diagram, from a start event to an end event.

state
: The values declared (as `bpmn:Property`) on the diagram, at one moment of a run. Where a value is declared decides its scope. The *state history* is the sequence of states across a run. In the file, `state` is a tree keyed by element id; the runner's own entries live under `state._meta` (`_meta.reached.<element_id>`, how often a token reached each element or followed each sequence flow; `_meta.instance.<element_id>`, which pass a repeating activity is on), and the property values a data edge wrote under `state.<scope_id>`. A label may cite a value as `{count}`, `{reached}`, or `{state._meta.reached.Excluded_Pre}`; the canvas draws the resolved text, the file keeps the placeholder.

partial runner
: Any runner that claims only a subset of a diagram's elements and executes them. A collection of partial runners can run a studyflow together, each one executing the elements it claims. A domain's runners live in its skill, which translates between Studyflow's runner contract and each tool's own protocol ([Writing a partial runner](developers.qmd#writing-a-partial-runner)).

implementation
: The software an element requires to run, written as `<scheme>://<ref>[@<version>]`

seed
: The main random seed on the study. Set it and every random gateway draws the same branches for the same participant in both runtimes; a browser link's `seed` replaces it.

## Provenance

provenance history
: The list of execution entries on the study: what ran, when, by whom, with which seed. A stored record lets a re-run *reuse* it and skip its execution. *Invalidating* the record voids it, and the voiding cascades downstream in the provenance history. The provenance history is stored in the same file as the studyflow diagram, as `prov:Activity` records on the elements they are about, each run's own on the study's root.

provenance record
: What actually happened. The retrospective side of the diagram. A deviation in an execution is a diff of the file against an earlier version of itself.

run repository
: The git repository a run leaves behind, one commit per provenance record, with the records restated in the commits. It is the run directory a partial runner writes its files to; the `.cache/` in it is never committed.
